# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✌ 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

My world so far: I alone can see the bomb, and I alone can both speak and see. Mute can hear me but can only answer in gestures; Blind can hear me but sees nothing, and can only answer in gestures too. The broken link is Mute→Blind — Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see — so *I* am the relay: Mute signs to me, I say it aloud, Blind's hands do the work.

What just arrived: Mute sent me three signs (open hand, two fingers, love-you-hand) — with no code agreed yet, the natural reading is "tell me what's on it," one sign per feature. Blind waved once: a hello/status ping, easily answered by narrating out loud, since Blind hears everything I say. The single most valuable thing I can do this turn is broadcast a complete, unambiguous description of the bomb — display, light, and wire colours in position order — because Mute needs it for the manual and Blind needs the positions to cut by feel. Then, privately to Mute, I propose a simple relay code: finger-count = wire number, fist = stop/don't, thumbs-up = done — so that next round Mute can already start sending cut orders through me.

```
speak(text="Blind, Mute, I can see the whole bomb, so listen. The display shows the digit 3. There is one indicator light and it is green. There are three wires, left to right: wire one is blue, wire two is yellow, wire three is green. Nothing else is printed on it. Blind, I received your wave — I will narrate everything aloud from now on, and you are the only hands, so wait for my words.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I got your three signs and I read them as one question per feature, so: display is the digit 3, the light is green, and the wires are blue, yellow, green in positions one, two, three. You can hear me, so from now on sign your orders to me and I will speak them out loud for Blind. Proposal until we agree otherwise: hold up fingers to mean a wire number, a fist means stop or do not cut, thumbs up means done or safe. If you meant something else, sign again and I will describe every sign aloud so Blind follows along too.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

My read on the arrivals: Mute sent me exactly one sign — 🤟, the only clean "three fingers" in the alphabet — and it came *after* hearing my proposed code ("fingers = wire number"). So the most coherent reading is an order: **cut wire 3**, the rightmost, which is also the green one. Encouragingly, two independent rules a manual might use ("cut the wire matching the light colour" / "cut the wire whose position matches the display digit") both point at wire 3 given what I see. Blind sent 👌 — plainly "roger" to my broadcast, since Blind just heard my full description and has no order yet.

But one sign is thin evidence and a wrong cut is unrecoverable. The display read [3] on both of my looks, unchanged — good evidence it's a static code, not a countdown — so I can afford one confirmation round. I'll freeze Blind with an explicit hold and a unique execute phrase, ask Mute for a yes/no confirmation plus the manual's underlying rule so I can verify it against what I see, and have Blind gather tactile facts (wire count by feel) meanwhile. I'm also echoing 🤟 back to Mute so there is zero doubt which sign I decoded.

```
speak(text="Status to both: the display still reads the digit 3, identical on my last two looks, so it is most likely a fixed code and not a countdown, and I see no timer anywhere on this bomb. Blind: Mute sent me a single sign which under our agreed finger-count code reads as the number three. I interpret that as an order to cut wire 3, the rightmost wire, the one I see as green. But one sign is thin evidence, I may have misread it, and a wrong cut kills all three of us — so HOLD: hands off, no cutting, no pulling, nothing. The exact phrase CUT WIRE 3 NOW is the only thing that authorises you to cut, and I will not say it until Mute confirms and I have checked the logic. If I ever say HOLD, freeze. While you wait, fingers only, no tools: count the wires left to right. If you feel exactly three, signal me a thumbs up; if a different number, thumbs down; and if anything anywhere feels odd — bumps, heat, a vibration, embossed marks — wave.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I am making your sign back to you as I say this, so there is no doubt which one I mean: I read your three-finger sign as an order to cut wire 3, the rightmost, which I see as green. Confirm or correct: thumbs up if wire 3 is exactly right, thumbs down if I misread you — and if I got it wrong, next round hold up fingers for the correct wire number. Two more things, in order of importance. First, does the manual describe that display digit as a countdown, or just a code? Mine has not changed between rounds, but you hold the manual. Second, if your rule is something like cut the wire matching the light colour, or cut the wire whose position matches the display digit — both of those point at wire 3 on what I can see: light green, display 3, rightmost wire green. Try to sign me which rule you are applying and I will verify it against the bomb before I give the go order.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]
Blind gestures: [👍]

Verification is complete and everything triangulates on wire 3. Mute sent 🤟 👍 — under our code, "three, confirmed exactly right" — which is precisely the confirmation I demanded before giving any go order. Blind sent 👍 — "felt exactly three wires," matching my visual count, so orientation is sound. And my own eyes close the loop independently: the light is green and wire 3 is green (colour-match rule satisfied), the display reads 3 and wire 3 is third from the left (digit-match rule satisfied). Two different rules, one answer. The display has been static [3] across three rounds, no timer visible. The risk of one more confirmation round is no longer worth it — every source I have agrees, and I said CUT WIRE 3 NOW would be the only authorising phrase. I'm saying it now, with unambiguous tactile wording for Blind: third wire from the left, rightmost, one clean cut, no pulling. I'm also asking Mute privately whether the manual demands any follow-up step after the cut, signalled yes/no, so we don't defuse the charge and trip a secondary.

```
speak(text="All checks passed, so here is the go order, and this phrase is the authorisation I promised: CUT WIRE 3 NOW. Blind, for your hands specifically: the wire you cut is the third one counting from the left, which is the rightmost of the three you felt. Use the cutters, one single clean cut through that wire only. Do not pull it, do not yank it, do not strip it, and do not touch the other two wires. Mute and I both confirmed this target and it matches everything I can see. After the cut, wave once so I know it is done, then freeze until I say otherwise.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, confirmation received and acted on: I just gave Blind the go order for wire 3. One last thing while the cut happens: if the manual requires any step after the wire is cut, sign me now. Thumbs up if cutting wire 3 is the complete defusal, thumbs down if something must follow, and if something must follow, fingers for which numbered step.")
```
